subject: Clarify: token rounding and long-context billing for Pinegrove pilot

Subject: Clarify: token rounding and long-context billing for Pinegrove pilot

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looks good. Before we lock the pilot SOW I need to confirm how Redwood will bill some of our expected usage patterns so we can model costs on our side. Two specific asks:

1) Long documents uploaded as a single prompt: we routinely send a 120k-character document (roughly 25k tokens) and then run multiple calls that reference the same context. Do you bill the full 25k tokens on every call, or is there a prefix/KV cache credit when the conversation references the same document repeatedly?

2) Rounding/minimums: our finance team needs a clear rule for partial-token handling and line-item quantum. If a request uses 3,450 tokens and your billing quantum is 1,000, do you round up to 4,000 tokens, or is there different behavior for streaming vs single-shot calls? Also curious about minimums per-call vs session pooling.

If you can send a sample invoice or a one-page worked example that shows the math for a few scenarios that would be ideal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is waiting for the cost modeling before the pilot approval next week.

Best,
Ellen
Head of ML Integrations
Pinegrove Analytics

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@pinegrove.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify: token rounding and long-context billing for Pinegrove pilot

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear questions, and great to meet yesterday. Below is a concise summary and a couple of worked examples; I’ve attached a short sample invoice and the spreadsheet with the calculations. Kimberly I’m looping you in to confirm EU-region rounding detail and any special pilot concessions. Sergio, FYI on cache semantics in case you want to add technical notes.

High level answers:
- KV/prefix caching: Redwood gives automatic prefix/KV cache credits for identical context reuse within an active conversation window. The cache credit reduces billed input tokens for subsequent calls that reuse the same token prefix; we bill only incremental tokens that are not satisfied from the KV cache.
- Billing quantum & rounding: Billing is computed per-request and then aggregated per-invoice line. For hosted API (default): we meter exact token counts but invoice items are rounded to the invoice quantum of 100 tokens. So a 3,450-token call shows as 3,500 tokens on the invoice (round up to nearest 100).
- Minimums: There is no per-call minimum for hosted pay-as-you-go; however, certain pilot reserved SKUs include a per-request floor (e.g., 1,000 token minimum). Reserved capacity (Dedicated) customers often have a configurable per-call floor for amortization; we can add a pilot override if you need it.

Worked examples (attached spreadsheet has step-by-step):
A) One-off call with long document (no cache reuse)
- Raw input tokens: 25,000
- Raw output tokens: 120
- Raw total: 25,120 -> invoice quantum rounding: 25,200
- Line item shows 25,200 tokens at the per-token rate

B) Repeated references (same prefix cached)
- First call: 25,000 input, 120 output -> invoice 25,200
- Second call referencing same doc, 60 new tokens of novel prompt + 80 output tokens that are different -> cache reduces billed input to 60 -> raw total 60+80=140 -> invoice rounded to 200 tokens
- Net for two calls: 25,200 + 200 = 25,400 total tokens billed

C) Streaming case (for session-like streaming)
- We meter tokens per chunk; rounding still happens at invoice-quantum level (100 tokens). For many small streaming chunks across a single session we also provide a session aggregation option for reserved customers to avoid repeated rounding inefficiency — happy to add this for your pilot if you expect many micro-chunks.

Attachments: billing-sample-7.pdf (sample invoice), pricing-math.xlsx (detailed calc).

If you’d like a one-page summary tailored to Pinegrove expected patterns (avg doc size, calls per doc, expected concurrency) I can run the numbers and include recommended SKU (hosted vs pilot reserved) + an estimated monthly cost range.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: billing-sample-7.pdf (PDF, 142 KB); pricing-math.xlsx (Excel, 36 KB))

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify: token rounding and long-context billing for Pinegrove pilot

Adding the EU nuance — for customers billed in EUR we currently keep the same token rounding quantum (100 tokens) but apply invoice aggregation at the region-billing level: multiple small calls within the same invoice period are aggregated before rounding when the customer is on a reserved monthly billing cycle. That means if Pinegrove takes a monthly reserved pilot in the EU we can reduce rounding inflation by aggregating all microcalls before applying the 100-token rounding.

Also important: KV cache credits are applied server-side before metering. If the prefix is identical token-for-token we zero out those tokens entirely. In practice we do not retroactively credit earlier invoices; cache benefits apply forward from the time the KV entries are warmed.

If Pinegrove wants to run a 14-day pilot we can enable session-level aggregation for the pilot (no extra charge) to show the difference in billing before you commit to reserved capacity.

Kimberly Park
Billing & Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
